title: aid-test-parallel-pilot-v1
description: The receipt from running one candidate lane both serially and concurrently in a disposable clone. It PROPOSES; it never writes the catalog, execution.yaml, or a scheduler mode. A promotion that is refused records the refusal — an absence would read as 'never tried'.

target_root.description: The disposable clone this ran in. Recorded so a reader can confirm it was not the live checkout.

membership.description: The exact run units piloted, sorted. A lane may only be promoted on evidence gathered for its OWN membership — this is what makes that checkable.

membership_sha256.description: Digest of the sorted membership. Required, and required to be checked against the lane it would promote: evidence gathered for one set may not promote another.

promotion.description: `proposed` means every repetition satisfied every criterion AND the measured benefit exceeded noise. `safe_not_worthwhile` means it was safe but not faster. `refused` means a criterion failed — and failure keeps units serial rather than being retried until green.

benefit_ms.description: Serial duration minus parallel duration, from the slowest repetition of each. Null when no repetition completed both runs.

failing_repetition.description: 1-based index of the first repetition that failed a criterion. Present exactly when promotion is `refused` for a per-repetition reason.

repetitions.description: One entry per repetition actually run. A `proposed` receipt must carry exactly `repeat` of them, all matching — otherwise a receipt claiming a benefit with an empty evidence list would validate, and a consumer that trusts `proposed` would promote a lane that never ran.

parallelism.description: Whether the runner could actually run cases concurrently. Bats delegates --jobs to GNU parallel; without it the flag degrades to serial, and a verdict drawn from that would describe a comparison that never happened.

results.description: Per-case outcomes, ordered. The comparison is over THIS, not over the aggregate verdict: a skip turning into a pass leaves the aggregate unchanged while changing what was actually verified.

dirty_paths.description: `git status --short` in the disposable root after the run. Non-empty means the run mutated tracked state, which no test lane may do.

escaped_paths.description: Entries that appeared beside the disposable root, from a pre-run/post-run inventory of its parent. A write outside the declared root is the failure mode a clone cannot contain.

differences.description: Named, never counted. 'three cases differed' sends nobody anywhere.

allOf.$comment: A proposal must rest on a measured benefit. Without one there is nothing to weigh against the risk of concurrency.
A refusal names which repetition failed, when the failure was per-repetition. A refusal with no locus is a verdict nobody can act on.
Nothing may be proposed when concurrency was unavailable: there was no concurrent run to draw a conclusion from.

A proposal must be backed by evidence: exactly `repeat` repetitions, every one a match, both sides exiting zero from a terminal_pass job. Without this a receipt with an empty `repetitions` array and a large `benefit_ms` validates, and 'consumes only proposed' promotes a lane nobody ran.
